**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/22 (Mon) 14:23  
[FACT] User has a 55-gallon aquarium.  
[FACT] User added their first batch of fish to the tank a month ago.  
[FACT] User's first batch of fish includes 10 neon tetras, 5 harlequin rasboras, and 1 small pleco.  
[FACT] User has been doing weekly water changes of 25%.  
[PREFERENCE] User likes the idea of adding rock caves and formations to the aquarium.  
[PREFERENCE] User is considering adding Corydoras catfish to the tank.  
[EVENT] User is planning to add Water Wisteria to the tank.  
[EVENT] User is planning to add driftwood to the tank.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Adding decorations can enhance the visual appeal of the tank and provide hiding places and territories for fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended decoration ideas include live plants, rock caves, driftwood, ornaments, plastic plants, substrate decorations, water features, hiding places, tunnels, and themed decorations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested low-maintenance live plants include Java moss, Anacharis, and Amazon swordplants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested adding 6-8 Corydoras catfish to the tank.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended smaller pleco species like Bristlenose plecos or Rubber Lip plecos, and other bottom-dwellers like Zebra loaches or Corydoras catfish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested monitoring water parameters, including ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate levels, before adding more fish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended increasing the frequency of water changes to maintain stable water parameters, especially with new additions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Water Wisteria prefers a temperature of 72°F to 82°F, a pH of 6.5 to 8.5, and medium to high lighting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested providing regular water changes, fertilizing plants, and pruning Water Wisteria for optimal growth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Driftwood can provide hiding places for plecos and Corydoras catfish.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended ensuring driftwood is boiled or soaked before adding it to the tank to prevent chemicals from leaching into the water.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested monitoring water circulation and ensuring the driftwood is securely anchored to prevent uprooting by fish.
